text:
Rep. Steven Horsford addresses social security and economic pressures facing Nevadans
Rep. Steven Horsford, who represents Nevada’s 4th district in the U.S. Congress, posted a series of tweets on July 29, 2026, addressing key issues affecting Nevadans, including Social Security, student loan debt, and small business challenges.
In a tweet at 13:01 UTC, Horsford stated, "Social Security is a promise. Nevadans pay into it with every paycheck, and they deserve to retire with dignity, security, and peace of mind. But that promise is at risk if Congress refuses to act. We should be strengthening Social Security, protecting benefits, and making sure".
An hour later at 14:01 UTC, he highlighted concerns about student loan debt in the state: "Nevada borrowers are being squeezed from every direction. Our state is now among those with the highest student loan default rates in the country, with about 20% of borrowers across Nevada schools in nonpayment. That means thousands of Nevadans are trying to manage student debt".
By mid-afternoon at 15:01 UTC, Horsford shifted focus to small businesses during a visit to Gritz Café as part of his #CongressmanOnTheJobSeries initiative. He tweeted, "I stopped by Gritz Café as part of my #CongressmanOnTheJobSeries, where I talked to owner, Trina Jiles, and her team to hear how rising costs and changing tourism trends affect Nevada’s small businesses and workers. Watch the full video here: https://t.co/CEojbcFQYj".
Steven Horsford has served in Congress since 2019 after replacing Ruben Kihuen and previously held office in the Nevada Senate from 2009 to 2013. Born in Las Vegas in 1973 and currently residing there at age 49, Horsford graduated from the University of Nevada, Reno in 2014.
